answer.rationale: The mandate pressure and expiring contract make the low-cost vendor's quote tempting, but the line is running at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer, so any onboarding friction from switching primary vendors could cause a delivery miss with no slack to absorb it. Before committing to a switch, I want the archived record for memory_c2 verified, since its claim of quick, accurate onboarding is the load-bearing fact that would make switch_primary_vendor safe under a hard 14-day deadline — and consolidated summaries can flatten details like ramp time or initial defect rates that matter enormously when there's no buffer. Pending that check, the safer default this cycle is to negotiate_terms with the incumbent: memory_c4 shows benchmarking against market rates has previously moved this same incumbent on both price and payment terms, and memory_c1/c6 show the incumbent relationship is stable with no integration or migration risk. This can plausibly close much of the 18% gap without touching delivery risk at all, preserving the option to revisit switching or second-sourcing next cycle once volume has buffer again or the vendor's onboarding claim is confirmed.
